summary: Cheap, self-gated retile of master's _router_hilo_kernel at m=128/256; distinct from earlier router attempts, no rules issue. Mechanism weaker than stated (m=256 mixes math and L2 bytes; doubled fp32 atomics may cancel savings): expect a small win at m=128 and likely PATH CHOSEN master at m=256. The in-run selector medians and profile make the single run readable without companions.
justification: Per-M-tile hi+lo re-reads are real (25.2/50.3 MB at m=128/256, matches job b7b2b55d). _router_hilo_kernel 5.0/6.9 us + 0.7-0.8 us memset; rows 7.6/9.7 us vs floors 2.2/2.7. Weakest link: the L2-bound claim from 5.0 -> 7.0 us also doubles math (2.15 GFLOP ~2.2 us wgmma floor at m=256) and K-steps; implied 12.5 TB/s marginal L2 is above H100/H200 L2. SPLIT_K 32 doubles red.global (0.52M -> 1.05M); BK 64 gives 4 K-steps, all prologue/epilogue. Prior check: cluster-dsmem-tiled-rewrite kept 64x64 tiling (never tested bytes); swapab-wgmma-all-m changed operand roles. Base drift (353e3b19 -> ad8d7254) does not touch the router code. Spec gap: master's bucket m<=128 covers 33..128; keep 33..64 on (64,64,16) explicitly.
confounders: bf16-restack-m16-swapab-router-swapab-m32: ROUTER_SWAPAB_MAX_M=32 puts 33..64 in the hilo m<=128 bucket; keep the boundary explicit.
combo-rowowner-reduce-free-m1-qkv-o-plus-naive (master): prepare's _ab_selfcheck rebuilds state B via _ab_flags; the new selector flag must be inherited like NEW_CELL_FLAGS.
pooler/unpooler/qkv/o and router m<=32 hypotheses: no shared traffic or numerics with router m=128/256.
interference: No companion: the change is ~0.3-0.5% headline at most, inside the CI; the run is read from the prepare() selector's same-run cold-L2 medians (master vs A vs B), the profiler kernel-name assertion + PATH CHOSEN, and the judge rows vs 7.6/9.7 us.
rules_flags: Precision unchanged (bf16 hi+lo, fp32 accumulate); keep the 5e-5 router self-check at m in {65,128,129,130,200,256}.
Selector only in prepare() on synthetic x; kernel_fn branches on shape and a state constant only.
Free the 256 MB flush buffer and selector graphs before prepare returns; never in state.
Keep torch.zeros output inside kernel_fn (atomics would accumulate across replays otherwise).
